title: He didn’t say, “Teach us to succeed.”
paragraphs: He didn’t say, “Teach us to succeed.”

Because we’ve built lives that don’t require God…
and then wonder why we feel empty when the noise dies down.

You can serve.
You can lead.
You can show up every Sunday.
But when was the last time you were alone with God… and stayed there?

Not rushing.
Not performing.
Not pretending.

We admire prayer…
but we avoid it.

We talk about God…
but we don’t talk to Him.

We know the language of faith…
but not the posture of surrender.
And that’s where the fracture begins.

Luke 11:1 says,
“Now Jesus was praying in a certain place, and when he finished, one of his disciples said to him, ‘Lord, teach us to pray…’”
Because they saw something in Jesus that exposed something in them.

They saw a man who withdrew when others pushed forward.
A man who knelt when others climbed.
A man who depended on the Father while everyone else depended on themselves.
Some of us don’t avoid prayer because we’re busy.
We avoid prayer because we’re ashamed.

Because when you get quiet…
you hear the truth.

The compromise.
The hidden sin.
The pride dressed up as purpose.

Because we’ve mastered looking strong…
but we don’t know how to be real.

Psalm 66:18 says,
“If I had cherished sin in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.”
That’s God exposing what’s blocking intimacy.

You can’t cling to sin
and expect closeness with God.

You can’t hold onto pride
and experience His presence.
But here’s where grace breaks in.

Romans 5:8 says,
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when you cleaned up your life.

You are more sinful than you want to admit…
but more loved than you can imagine.
And Jesus didn’t just die to forgive your sin.
He died to restore your access.

Hebrews 4:16 says,
“Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace…”
Through Jesus, the door to the Father is not cracked open.
You don’t need to impress God.
You need to come to Him.

Your guilt.
Your addiction.
Your anxiety.
Your numbness.
Because prayer is not where you prove your worth.
Prayer is where you admit your need.
Some scholars interpret the Lord’s Prayer not just as a template—but as a reordering of the heart.

“Hallowed be Your name…”
God above self.
Prayer is not about getting God to move.
And some of you feel that tension right now.

You still believe in God…
but you don’t feel Him anymore.
God did not move away from you.

James 4:8 says,
“Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you.”
And whisper the most dangerous prayer you can pray:

Teach me to pray when I don’t feel like it.
Teach me to seek You when I’d rather scroll.
Teach me to want You more than my sin.
In the place where no one sees…
